title: [v0.4.x] Quality: staticcheck, govulncheck and risk-focused tests
author: mcpdev80
body:
Parent acceptance: #174 (v0.4.31 final semantic acceptance); initial integration/ratchet starts with #872 (v0.4.25). This is a **standalone, bounded quality work package**, not a general refactor and not a prerequisite to reopening v0.4.24.

## Goal
Introduce reproducible, low-noise static analysis, vulnerability checks and targeted coverage for BaseHarbor before the v0.5 contract freeze. Developer UX first; smallest useful gates; no needless CI churn.

## Package A: staticcheck
- Add a reproducibly version-pinned `staticcheck` version compatible with the repository's Go toolchain.
- Run targeted/local checks first; integrate into an appropriate existing CI workflow with useful diagnostics and caching.
- Fix actionable new findings on changed code; for legacy findings adopt a documented, shrinking baseline or narrowly justified suppressions rather than sweeping edits. Avoid formatting-only churn.
- `go vet ./...` stays active; lint augments rather than replaces it.
- Only run `golangci-lint` if a concrete need remains; no mandatory second lint framework for its own sake.

## Package B: govulncheck
- Use a version-pinned `govulncheck` against Go modules/package paths; document precise reproducible local command.
- Gate on actionable, reachable vulnerabilities; document non-reachable/inconclusive advisories separately. Provide version/advisory/fix/evidence and exceptions with owners/review dates, never silently ignore.
- Respect GitHub workflow permissions and existing supply-chain conventions; avoid introducing extra secrets or external credential dependencies.

## Package C: risk-focused tests & coverage
- Measure **actual** package/function coverage before deciding targets. A claimed 0% unit figure is not by itself proof of no runtime test coverage.
- Prioritize uncovered **real decision logic and failure paths** in `health`, `providers/runtime/docker`, `provideroperation`, `providerui`, `stableid`, `database`, `exposure`, as applicable on the current v0.4.25 tree.
- Most important cross-cutting acceptance: shared vs app-scoped ownership isolation, HA off-by-default, TLS always, configured-only destroy without deployed Core, cleanup and preservation, backup/recovery, and typed CLI/MCP errors.
- Use focused table-driven tests and negative cases (missing Core, partial state, wrong owner, retry/idempotency, disconnected provider). Keep runtime-dependent gates separate from pure unit packages; don't pretend opt-in integration has run when it hasn't.
- Establish **per-package, non-regressing coverage baselines for selected high-risk packages** and a small documented target for improvement. Avoid a single global coverage threshold and avoid brittle tests for generated adapters.

## Developer workflow & CI acceptance
- Provide one discoverable documented local entry point (script or make target if warranted) to run fast static/vuln/coverage checks, ideally matching CI commands. No need to add Makefile solely for points.
- Reuse existing atomic gates and Hugging Face for fast tests where available; use Actions sparingly for compatible OS/runtimes. Do not run Docker/Podman/K3s release matrices just to qualify static analysis.
- Pin tool versions, ensure deterministic success/failure and helpful error text; document in EN/DE.
- Evidence: workflow links with SHA, before/after coverage numbers per selected package, actual findings and remediation/waivers, duration and noise impacts, all tests green. No fake green from skipped checks.
- Scope discipline: no large-scale package consolidation, new providers, HA/recovery redesign, unrelated refactors or changes to Kubernetes roadmap.
- Introduce the bounded gates as early as practical starting with the v0.4.25 candidate; retain them in each later release. Final cross-package completion belongs to #174 / v0.4.31. No release, tagging or merge without separately authorized release process.

## Definition of done
1. staticcheck repeatably green with reviewed baseline; Go vet unchanged.
2. govulncheck repeatably green for applicable reachable vulnerabilities, with documented management of non-actionable findings.
3. Measured improvement and regression protection in targeted high-risk Go packages; representative negative tests.
4. Local fast-check command and CI parity, EN/DE documentation.
5. Evidence (SHA, tests, runtime boundaries), no unnecessary full-suite repetitions.

Derived from technical assessment on **release/v0.4.21**: listed coverage numbers and tool gaps must be reverified on the actual v0.4.25 branch rather than assumed current.

---

## Release assignment update (2026-10-10)
**Do not defer quality to the end:** establish minimal version-pinned actionable staticcheck/govulncheck and focused risk coverage as early as practical starting v0.4.25 #872; apply them as a non-regressing ratchet in every subsequent release. #862's final cross-package completion/evidence and quality acceptance belongs under #174/v0.4.31. Old v0.4.25-only title is superseded; no CI spam or full reruns just for static checks.
